title: Majestic Knights
transcript: White's brilliant idea is knight to e3 check, attacking the king and the bishop at the same time. But this doesn't seem to make sense. This allows the king to take one of the white pawns, and now this knight is hanging, and so is this one. And there is a pawn that is running towards promotion. But white did have an idea in mind. He can now take the bishop on d5, and surprisingly enough, if the king takes, after knight to b6, there is going to be a fork of the king and the pawn, meaning that white will be left with an extra knight. And this is going to be winning. But this shouldn't bother black. Instead of capturing the knight back, he can simply start to run with pawn to a3. Both c3 and b4 are defended by the black pieces, so this knight cannot stop the pawn. In desperation, white plays knight a to c7, bringing the knight closer and defending the other one. But black simply runs, and is now only one square away from getting a new queen. So, is this it? Is white simply lost in this position? Well, not exactly. White has an absolutely majestic idea in this position that starts with a knight b5, giving a check and re-sacrificing the other knight. But what's really weird about this move is not the fact that the knight is hanging, because it is pretty clear that if the knight is taken, knight to c3 is going to fork the king and pawn, and this is still winning for white. What is surprising is that the king can just move and maintain an attack on both knights while still threatening the promotion. And although white can play one of the knights to c3 because they defend each other, this is still too slow. But knight to b5 was only the first of two incredible moves that white had planned. And a shiver goes down the spine of the player with the black pieces as he sees the brilliant king to e4, a quiet, patient, and beautiful move that still leaves a knight hanging. But of course, the knight still cannot be taken because of the fork. But this seems to lose to a1 queen and the truth is that yes, this position would be lost in every universe but this one because what black failed to realize is that in this position knight d6 is one of the most peculiar checkmates that I have ever seen.
